back: How many of a product are made and how often — it decides the materials, processes, machinery, labour and cost per product.
As more are made, the cost per product falls, because set-up costs are shared and materials are bought in bulk.
A single product made to a client's exact needs, often by hand. Unique and high quality but slow and very costly — bespoke furniture, prototypes.
A set quantity of identical products made at one time, possibly repeated. Flexible, but machines are idle while reset — bread, furniture ranges.
Very large numbers of identical products on a production line. Low cost per item but huge set-up cost and inflexible — cars, phones.
Materials and components arrive from suppliers exactly when they are needed on the production line, instead of being stored.
Less money tied up in stock, less storage and waste — but production stops if a delivery is late; relies on reliable suppliers.
Production running 24/7 making very high volumes on automated lines — drinks cans, bottles, screws, paper.
Lowest cost per item, consistent quality, few workers — but huge investment, one breakdown halts everything, no flexibility.

front: Why is CAM important in high-volume production?
back: Consistent, interchangeable parts; continuous running; complex shapes repeated; reprogrammable; less waste; robots do dangerous tasks.
Designing products to fit the people who use them so they are comfortable, safe and efficient.
The measurement of the human body, collected as data and used for ergonomic decisions.

front: Which percentile for a shelf, and for a doorway?
back: A shelf must be reachable by a 5th percentile user; a doorway must clear a 95th percentile user.
Users vary a lot in size, so office chairs, car seats and bike saddles are adjustable to fit most people.
The UK's national strategic adviser on design — an independent charity founded in 1944 that promotes design to improve business, public services and lives.
The Design Council's design process: Discover, Define, Develop, Deliver.
A team of multi-skilled workers and machines in a cell makes a complete product or component and shares responsibility for quality.
Removing every kind of waste — stock, waiting, unnecessary movement, overproduction and defects. JIT is part of it.
Consider quantity, whether it is unique, whether demand is steady or seasonal, whether tooling costs can be recovered, and the selling price.
